headline: Common Myths About DIY Garage Fire Restoration
articleBody: When a garage fire hits, it's natural to want to roll up your sleeves and get things back to normal fast. But there are a few common myths about DIY fire restoration that can actually do more harm than good. Myth 1: Regular household cleaners will get rid of smoke and soot. Fact: Nope! Soot and smoke are acidic and greasy, and typical cleaners can smear them, driving them deeper into porous surfaces or setting stains permanently. You need specialized products. Myth 2: Just airing out the garage will remove the smoke smell. Fact: While ventilation helps initially, smoke particles embed themselves in walls, insulation, and belongings. Without professional odor removal techniques, that smell will likely return, especially on humid days. Myth 3: If it looks clean, it’s safe. Fact: Fire damage can compromise structural integrity, and smoke can leave behind invisible, corrosive residues that continue to damage materials over time. Plus, inhaling these residues isn't good for your health. Myth 4: I can handle the water damage from the fire department myself. Fact: Extinguishing a fire often leaves significant water behind. If not dried completely and quickly, you're inviting mold growth, which creates a whole new problem. For thorough and safe cleanup, it's best to call in experts like First To Respond Restoration. We’re available 24/7 and have the certified technicians and proper tools to tackle any level of fire damage.
